chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Sukayn and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

It was said to him, 'So-and-so was afflicted with major ritual impurity (janabah), and he was a person with pockmarks (majdur). So they washed him, and he died.' He said: 'They killed him. Why did they not ask? Why did they not perform tayammum? Indeed, the cure for the ailment is asking (for guidance).'
He said, 'And that is reported regarding the one with a broken limb, and the one with internal illness: they perform tayammum and do not perform ghusl.'

key_terms.مَجْدُورٌ: A person with pockmarks or smallpox scars, often implying sensitivity to water

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person with janabah who has a skin condition or injury that makes washing harmful?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the principle of 'la darar wa la dirar' (no harm) in fiqh, illustrating that forcing a janabah state upon a patient with a debilitating condition (majdur) constitutes a form of homicide due to ignorance of the alternative, tayammum. It underscores the practical necessity of consulting scholars to adapt ritual purity rules to individual medical circumstances, a key feature of Shia juristic methodology. The narration serves as a foundational precedent for prioritizing preservation of life and health over rigid adherence to standard washing procedures.
